title: Modalverben
concept: können, müssen, wollen, dürfen, sollen, möchten

learn.heading: Six helper verbs
learn.text: Modal verbs express ability, duty, wish or permission. They are irregular in the **singular**: **ich** and **er/sie/es** have **no ending** and the same form. The plural is regular. Learn the six forms of each verb together, and notice that *möchten* is a polite form that you will use every day.

examples.en: You have to get up early tomorrow.
We would like to go hiking at the weekend.

learn.heading: Word order: the infinitive goes to the end
learn.text: The modal verb is the conjugated verb, so it is in **position 2**. The main verb stays in the **infinitive and goes to the very end** of the sentence. This creates a frame: *Ich **kann** heute nicht ins Kino **gehen**.* In questions, the modal comes first (yes/no) or after the question word. You may leave out the main verb when the meaning is clear: *Ich muss nach Hause.*

examples.en: I have to work late today.

examples.de: Was möchtest du am Wochenende machen?
examples.en: What would you like to do at the weekend?

learn.heading: Meanings and everyday use
learn.text: **können** = can (ability, possibility). **müssen** = must, have to. **wollen** = want (strong). **möchten** = would like (polite, softer than *wollen*). **dürfen** = may, be allowed to. **sollen** = should, ought to (a rule or what someone told you). For polite requests use **Können Sie …?** or **Könnten Sie …?** *Nicht dürfen* means "must not", while *nicht müssen* means "don't have to".

examples.de: Der Arzt sagt, ich soll mehr schlafen.
examples.en: The doctor says I should sleep more.

tip: Think of the frame "modal ... infinitive": the modal is like a left bracket in position 2 and the infinitive is the right bracket at the end. Fill the middle with everything else.

exercises.explain: ich kann: the singular has no ending.
du musst: müssen is irregular in the singular.
er/sie/es has the same form as ich: kann.
The plural wir takes the infinitive form.
darf for ich. A yes/no question puts the modal first.

exercises.q: Der Arzt sagt, ich ___ mehr schlafen. (sollen)

exercises.explain: Modal in position 2, infinitive at the end.

exercises.q: How do you politely order a coffee?
exercises.explain: möchten is the polite form; wollen sounds too demanding.

options: You don't have to smoke here.

exercises.explain: Learn the modals as a set of six; möchten is the polite wish.
Modal in position 2, infinitive arbeiten at the end.
Yes/no question: modal first, infinitive at the end.

exercises.answer: Am Samstag will ich ins Kino gehen
exercises.explain: Position 1 is the time, the modal stays in position 2, and the infinitive goes last.

exercises.en: I would like to meet friends at the weekend.
answer: Ich möchte am Wochenende Freunde treffen
Am Wochenende möchte ich Freunde treffen
exercises.explain: möchte + infinitive treffen at the end.

shadow.de: Kannst du am Samstag mit ins Kino kommen?
shadow.en: Can you come to the cinema with us on Saturday?

shadow.de: Ich kann leider nicht, ich muss arbeiten.
shadow.en: Unfortunately I can't, I have to work.

shadow.de: Wir möchten am Sonntag im Park Fußball spielen.
shadow.en: We'd like to play football in the park on Sunday.

shadow.de: Darf ich Ihnen eine Frage stellen?
shadow.en: May I ask you a question?

shadow.de: Was möchtest du heute Abend machen?
shadow.en: What would you like to do this evening?

prompts.hint: Ich möchte … / Ich kann am … / Ich muss …
